title: Security gates sequencing & retention — go/no-go checklist for MAP sprint
text:
Security gates sequencing & retention — go/no-go checklist for MAP sprint

['From: Elena Soto <elena@finarc.com>
To: soojin_lee@redwood.ai
Cc: FinArc Security Team <security@finarc.com>, Marco Li <marco.li@procure.finarc.com>
Date: 2028-03-18T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: MAP — security gates & retention sequencing

Hi Soojin,

Thanks for walking through the platform last week. Procurement asked me to document the acceptance path so their legal and controls teams can sign off. We want a concise mutual action sprint (2-week window) that clearly lists the security/compliance gates and the minimal evidence required for each gate so legal can prioritize redlines.

Key asks from FinArc:
- SOC 2: latest report + list of control owners and timeframe for us to validate a subset of controls (logs/incident mgmt).
- SIG / CAIQ: gap items that would block production access. If you can highlight items typically deferred to SOC or archival controls, that helps.
- DPA: data retention defaults (hosted vs private), required annex for EU data, and escrow/segregation language.
- Go/no-go criteria and final signoff owner (who at Redwood confirms we can flip prod access).

Can you send a short checklist (one page preferred) and an outline of the evidence delivery timeline? We need to present this to our CISO on Monday.

Regards,
Elena Soto
Security Program Manager
FinArc
', 'From: soojin_lee@redwood.ai
To: Elena Soto <elena@finarc.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-03-18T11:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: MAP — security gates & retention sequencing

Elena — thanks, and great to meet you last week. Below is a compact MAP sprint checklist plus a proposed evidence cadence. I kept each gate to the minimal artifacts FinArc typically requests for a production enablement decision. Happy to trim further for your CISO slide.

One-page MAP sprint checklist (summary):
1) SOC 2 readiness (Gate A) — deliverables: SOC 2 Type II report (PDF), list of control owners + contact, three example audit trails for logging/incident response. Decision criteria: SOC 2 report with opinion covering last 12 months OR documented remediation plan with target dates and temporary compensating controls.

2) SIG / CAIQ assessment (Gate B) — deliverables: completed CAIQ spreadsheet, highlighted high/critical gaps, remediation ETA for any high gaps. Decision criteria: No outstanding critical SIG items blocking network or data isolation; medium items accepted with remediation commit.

3) DPA & retention annex (Gate C) — deliverables: Draft DPA with retention table (hosted default = 90 days transient logs, 7 years customer data per request vs 30/60 day options), EU data annex if applicable, redline-ready doc. Decision criteria: Mutually agreed DPA text for core controls and retention window agreed in MAP or escalated to legal for final signoff.

4) Access & environment controls (Gate D) — deliverables: environment topology diagram (hosted/dedicated/private), encryption-at-rest proof, key management description (KMS/HSM option). Decision criteria: Topology and KMS option accepted or plan for private deployment scheduled before production.

Go/no-go: Production access granted when Gates A–C are green and Gate D is either green or has an agreed mitigation/rollout plan (canary-only). Final signoff: Ben Carter (Sales Ops) + Marissa Cole (Customer Security Liaison) to provide green check; legal signoff to confirm DPA execution.

Proposed 2-week evidence cadence (high level):
- Day 1: SOC 2 report + CAIQ baseline + DPA draft (Redline v1)
- Day 3: Redwood provides control owner list and environment diagram
- Day 5: FinArc questions on CAIQ highlights (sync call)
- Day 8: Redwood delivers remediation plan for any high gaps + updated DPA (redlines addressed)
- Day 10: Legal review by both sides; apply final DPA comments
- Day 14: Final signoff / canary enablement

Attachments: SOC2-report-2027.pdf (stub), SIG-CAIQ-self-assessment.xlsx (stub), initial_DPA_v2.docx (stub) — sending in separate email for clarity.

If this works I’ll loop in Laura (legal) to accelerate DPA comments and propose a short working call tomorrow.

Thanks — Soojin
Soojin Lee
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
', "From: ben_carter@redwood.ai
To: soojin_lee@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-03-18T13:20:00-07:00
Subject: Internal: FinArc MAP sprint — prep notes

Looping in legal early. A couple of internal notes before we send the attachments to FinArc:
- Laura: be prepared for a proposed 7-year customer retention clause — they sometimes push that for archived records. We should propose a tiered approach (90-day transaction logs by default; up to 7 years on request with escrow/legal approval).
- Marissa: you'll drive the CAIQ call. Prioritize network segmentation and key mgmt items; if they ask about KV caching/prefix caching we should classify that as application-level (not persistence).
- Ops: ensure we can provide example audit trails stripped of PII — easiest ask for SOC 2 confirmation.

I’ll stand by for the DPA redline once Laura gives the green light.

—Ben", 'From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Marco Li <marco.li@procure.finarc.com>, Elena Soto <elena@finarc.com>
Cc: soojin_lee@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-03-19T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: RE: DPA initial redlines and retention table

Marco / Elena — attaching a redline of the DPA (redlined_DPA_v3.docx stub). Key points from our side:
- Retention: propose default data retention windows (Host: 90 days for ephemeral logs, 2 years for aggregated telemetry, customer-requested exports retain per contract up to 7 years).
- EU annex: we can add an EU-data addendum mirroring standard SCCs and clarify subprocessors.
- Escrow: we do not typically escrow customer data; we are open to negotiated escrow for high-need regulated customers under a commercial addendum.
- Liability carveouts: kept as-is but willing to discuss cap in line with deal size.

Please review the redline and flag must-haves. If FinArc needs an earlier production window we can scope a canary with restricted features while finalizing DPA.

Laura Bennett
Head of Legal, Redwood Inference
', 'From: Elena Soto <elena@finarc.com>
To: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, soojin_lee@redwood.ai
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, Marco Li <marco.li@procure.finarc.com>
Date: 2028-03-21T16:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: MAP sprint — acceptance path and DPA redline received

Laura / Soojin — thanks for the clear checklist and the DPA redline. Reviewed with our CISO — a few clarifying asks, none are blockers:
1) Can you confirm the 90-day default for ephemeral logs covers diagnostic logs only and not customer content?
2) For SOC 2 evidence, we only need audit trail samples (anonymized) for three incidents in the last 12 months.
3) CAIQ: we’ll accept medium items with remediation plans; agree high/critical must be addressed.

We’d like the canary plan enabled after Gates A–B are green and DPA language for retention is agreed in principle (legal to finish exact phrasing). If you can confirm Q1 and send the anonymized audit trails by EOD tomorrow, we’ll be ready to move into the 2-week sprint.

Thanks — Elena
